summary.text: This opportunity briefing explores combining global local attention, transformer architectures, and decoders for audio-visual speech separation and sequence generation. By incorporating global-local attention blocks into transformer decoder layers, the system efficiently captures multi-scale dependencies while reducing computational costs. Evidence suggests this combination achieves strong performance on sequence tasks while maintaining lower parameter requirements than traditional baselines.

target_user.text: The target user includes machine learning engineers, researchers, and developers building voice agents, speech processing pipelines, or multi-modal generation systems.

jtbd.text: When building speech processing or sequence generation pipelines, the user wants to efficiently capture multi-scale context without incurring excessive computational overhead so that high-performance models can run in resource-constrained environments.

value_prop.text: Integrating global-local attention into transformer decoders enables models to process complex multi-scale inputs with significantly fewer parameters and reduced computational complexity compared to standard full-attention architectures.

riskiest_assumption.text: Given the feasibility score of 2.0 on axis F, the riskiest assumption is that integrating global-local attention blocks into transformer decoder layers will maintain stable training dynamics and convergence without introducing severe gradient interference or custom kernel bottlenecks.

mvp.text: Build a technical proof of concept using existing packages by constructing a small transformer decoder model in Hugging Face Transformers that incorporates a global-local attention layer, and evaluate its training stability and inference latency on a standard sequence benchmark with a proposed threshold of 10 percent latency reduction compared to a baseline full-attention decoder.
mvp.type: technical proof of concept from existing packages

success_metric.text: Achieve a proposed threshold of at least 20 percent reduction in inference MACs or GPU memory usage while maintaining validation loss within a proposed threshold of 2 percent of a standard full-attention transformer baseline.

kill_criteria.text: The model fails to converge or exhibits higher validation loss than the baseline after a proposed threshold of 5 epochs of training.
Inference latency or memory consumption exceeds the baseline full-attention model by a proposed threshold of 5 percent during sequence generation.

open_source.use: Provides the foundational transformer model definitions and decoder building blocks.
Used to support efficient distributed training and memory-optimized execution of the model.

to_build.text: Custom global-local attention modules configured to operate natively within transformer decoder layers.
